traits: Cap 5 to 10 cm, pale then pink-ochre, wine-pink or purple-brown, often marbled with olive or rust patches
The skin stops short of the margin, so the gills "show their teeth"
Gills white to cream, close, forked near the stem, rust-spotted with age
Stem 2 to 10 cm, firm, white, sometimes tinged pink, browning at the base
Firm white flesh, mild taste with a nutty note
Under broadleaf trees, especially oaks, on light acid soil · July to October, sometimes from May
safetyNote: Good edible (Wikipedia, fr); the DGfM and the VAPKO list it. Rubbing the stem with ferrous sulfate turns it salmon (Wikipedia, en). Wikipedia (fr) names among its look-alikes the charcoal burner and the olive brittlegill (see their cards). The Belgian poison centre names the sickener among the russulas that cause a mild gastrointestinal illness.
